concepts.name: v_θ — the velocity network
concepts.summary: v_θ takes a noisy input, a scalar t and conditioning, and returns a velocity of the SAME shape — (32,32,4) in, (32,32,4) out. It is a U-Net or a DiT, architecturally identical to the diffusion noise-predictor; SD3 uses a DiT. Only two things changed from diffusion: the target (velocity x₁ − x₀ instead of noise ε) and the path (linear instead of the ᾱ schedule). The architecture must satisfy three requirements — shape-preserving, accepts a scalar t through a scaled sinusoidal timestep embedding, and accepts conditioning via cross-attention or adaLN — which is exactly the interface a noise-predictor already exposes, so the two are interchangeable.

concepts.name: Classifier-free guidance on velocities
concepts.summary: The same extrapolation as classifier-free guidance in diffusion, performed on velocities: ṽ = v_θ(x,t,∅) + w·[v_θ(x,t,c) − v_θ(x,t,∅)]. Start at the unconditional velocity, measure the difference the condition makes, and travel w times further along it; w=1 recovers the conditional velocity exactly and larger w pushes harder toward the prompt at the cost of saturation and diversity. Training still requires dropping the conditioning on about 10% of examples so one network learns both fields, and sampling still costs two forward passes per step — affordable here because flow matching takes about 10 steps rather than 1000.
